items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Gus had known the Scott orchestra before I joined it and he was very fond of Lloyd, Cecil and the other members that had been and those that were now with the orchestra.

ctx.x: We started going to Pittsburg, Pennsylvania and playing dances there and in Duquesne and mining towns not too far from Pittsburg. In most large cities or I should say in every large city in the country, there was wide open vice. Bootleg whisky, home brew, gambling and prostitution. Pittsburgh was jumping and Wiley Avenue was the main drag for the pimps, musicians and hustlers. We stayed at a hotel in Wiley Avenue and ate in a big restaurant near by, which was owned by a fellow named Gus Greenly.

Gus had known the Scott orchestra before I joined it and he was very fond of Lloyd, Cecil and the other members that had been and those that were now with the orchestra. Gus also had a gambling place next door to the restaurant and there was always a thousand dollars in silver dollar pieces stacked on the crap shooting table. Lloyd Scott was the only one in the orchestra that liked to gamble. He very seldom won anything.

With Gus in our corner we had nothing to worry about if we did not make much money working around Pittsburgh, because our credit was good in his restaurant. He would lend the orchestra his personal car if we needed transportation and he would bail us out if we could not pay our rent in the hotel who's owner was a friend of his.
